meta.label: Secondhand and resale
tradeoffLabels: seller keeps more of the sale price
buyer is protected if something goes wrong
meta.attribution: Fee figures and protection terms come from each marketplace's own published fee policy, seller agreement or buyer protection page, read directly, plus TheRealReal's 2025 annual report filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Dollar thresholds and percentages are the ones each platform states for US sellers and buyers, except for HEWI and Oxfam (UK) and Sellpy (EU, read from its German pricing page); a platform operating in other countries may set different figures there. Brand take-back programs such as Patagonia Worn Wear and lululemon Like New pay for trade-ins in store credit, often a small share of the original price, so their fee score reflects that credit rather than a cash commission. These fees change without much notice, several of the platforms scored here changed their fee structure at least once in the last two years, so check the linked page before relying on a number here. A high buyer protection score describes the strength of the guarantee as the platform itself states it, not an independent audit of how often claims are honored. Two routes cost nothing at all: giving clothes away through the Buy Nothing Project or Freecycle, and donating them to a charity thrift shop such as Goodwill, which pays the donor no cash but funds job training programs from what it resells. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Low seller fees, seller keeps more of the sale
Buyer protection if an item is fake, damaged or never arrives
Easy and immediate, without listing or shipping

products.name: eBay
products.description: A general online marketplace that sells clothing alongside almost everything else, by auction or fixed price, shipped by the seller after the item sells.

fees.note: eBay's own selling fees page states the final value fee for most categories, including general clothing, is 13.6% of the total sale amount up to $7,500 per item, plus a per-order fee of $0.30 for orders of $10 or less and $0.40 for orders over $10. Women's handbags carry a separate 15% fee (9% above $2,000), and athletic shoes have their own tiered rate.

buyer_protection.note: eBay's Money Back Guarantee page states coverage is automatic on virtually every purchase, covers the purchase price plus original shipping, and that there is no extra fee for the coverage. Separately, eBay's own Authenticity Guarantee page states eligible apparel items priced $200 and over from listed brands are physically inspected by experts before being shipped to the buyer.

products.name: Poshmark
products.description: A peer-to-peer app built around a social feed, where sellers photograph and price their own clothes and buyers can follow individual sellers' closets.

fees.note: Poshmark's own fee policy page states that after an item sells it deducts a small fee from the final order price: a flat $2.95 for sales under $15, and 20% for sales of $15 and above, so the seller keeps 80% on those sales.

buyer_protection.note: Poshmark's own Posh Protect page states buyers get a full refund if their item never ships or does not match the listing, and lists undisclosed damage, incorrect or missing items, and items that are not authentic as covered reasons, with 72 hours from delivery to report. The same page says a buyer cannot return an item under Posh Protect just because it is not their style or does not fit.

products.name: Depop
products.description: A peer-to-peer marketplace popular with younger sellers, built around individual shop pages rather than one combined catalog search.

fees.note: Depop's own seller fees article states no Depop selling fee is charged to sellers based in the UK, US or Australia. A US seller instead pays only the Depop Payments processing fee of 3.3% plus $0.45 per transaction, charged on the item price, shipping and any tax. Sellers outside those three countries pay a flat 10% selling fee.

buyer_protection.note: Depop's own Depop Protection page states a buyer gets a full refund, including shipping, fees and tax, if an item does not arrive, arrives damaged, or is significantly not as described, if reported within 30 days of purchase, for buyers in the UK, US and Australia who paid through Depop Payments. The same page states Depop Protection 'is not an insurance policy, a warranty, or a guarantee' and is granted at Depop's discretion.

products.name: Mercari
products.description: A general peer-to-peer marketplace for clothing and almost anything else, with a single flat selling fee and, since January 2025, no separate buyer payment fee.

fees.note: Mercari's help center states a 10% selling fee applies to the combined item price and buyer-paid shipping, for listings created or updated on or after January 6, 2025, and that Mercari no longer charges buyers a separate payment processing fee on those listings.

buyer_protection.note: Mercari's Buyer Protection page states a buyer can get a refund if the item is not as described in the listing, but must report the issue within 72 hours of confirmed delivery; after that window the payment is automatically released to the seller and the sale is final.

products.name: Vinted
products.description: A peer-to-peer clothing marketplace that charges sellers no fee at all, funding its buyer guarantee instead through a fee added to what the buyer pays.

fees.note: Vinted's own help page states there are no fees for uploading items or selling them on Vinted, and that once a sale closes the seller receives the full selling price straight to their Vinted Wallet.

buyer_protection.note: Vinted's own Buyer Protection page states a buyer is refunded if an item doesn't arrive, arrives damaged, or is significantly not as described, but must press 'I have an issue' within 2 days of the item being marked delivered, or the payment is automatically released to the seller. This is funded by a mandatory Buyer Protection fee added to every order at checkout, typically around 5% of the item price plus $0.70.

products.name: ThredUp
products.description: A mail-in consignment service. The seller sends a bag or box of clothes and ThredUp decides what to accept, prices it, lists it, and pays a percentage of whatever it sells for.

fees.note: ThredUp's own Clean Out earnings page shows a sliding payout scale set by ThredUp, not the seller: items that resell for $0.15 to $3 pay 3% to 15% of the sale price, $3 to $15 pay 15% to 30%, $15 to $60 pay 30% to 60%, $60 to $160 pay 60% to 80%, and $160 and up pay 80%.

accessibility.note: ThredUp's own Clean Out page states shipping bags and labels are always free, a bag holds up to 30 pounds and arrives within about a week, and the seller drops it at any UPS location. The same page states 'We price your items. Our algorithms set prices based on past sales, brand, and item quality,' so the seller does not photograph, write up or price each item.

products.name: The RealReal
products.description: A luxury consignment marketplace that authenticates every item before it is accepted for sale, taking a larger share of lower-priced items and a smaller share of high-value ones.

fees.note: TheRealReal's 2025 annual report, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, states consignors can earn up to 90% of the proceeds from the sale of their consigned items in commissions and achieved an overall commission rate of approximately 62% in 2025.

buyer_protection.note: TheRealReal's 2025 annual report states all consigned items pass through a brand-specific authentication process before they are accepted for consignment, each piece sold comes with an authentication certificate, and the company has 'a zero-tolerance policy when it comes to counterfeit goods,' with items found to be counterfeit removed from its authentication centers before reaching a buyer.

products.name: Grailed
products.description: A marketplace focused on menswear, streetwear and designer clothing, where sellers list their own items and some listings carry an authentication badge after review.

fees.note: Grailed's own fee page states the seller commission is 9% on sales of $120 or more, and a reduced 6% (minimum $1.99) on sales under $120 for sales on or after May 20, 2026, charged separately from a payment processing fee.

buyer_protection.note: Grailed's own Purchase Protection page states a buyer is covered if the item received is deemed inauthentic by Grailed, materially differs from its description, or is the wrong item, but issues must be reported within 3 calendar days of the item being received.

products.name: StockX
products.description: A marketplace built around a live bid-and-ask price, best known for sneakers but also selling streetwear and apparel, where almost every order is physically inspected before it ships to the buyer.

fees.note: StockX's own help page states Verified Marketplace sellers pay a 3% payment processing fee plus a base transaction fee that starts at 9% for a Level 1 seller and falls as low as 7% for a Level 5 seller who meets higher sales requirements, so a new seller pays about 12% combined.

buyer_protection.note: StockX's own help pages state its verification team inspects an item against StockX's condition guidelines before it ships to the buyer, and that the StockX Buyer Promise protects an order that 'arrives materially different from what was described,' with 14 days to report and a full refund if StockX cannot find a replacement after an item fails verification.

products.name: Vestiaire Collective
products.description: A global luxury resale marketplace that runs a digital authenticity check on every listing and offers an optional paid physical authentication and quality control service.

fees.note: Vestiaire Collective's own help page states a 12% selling fee applies to items priced between $83 and $16,667, plus a 3% (minimum $3) payment processing fee; items priced under $83 carry a fixed $10 charge instead.

buyer_protection.note: For an item bought from a private seller with Direct Shipping, Vestiaire Collective's own help page gives the buyer 72 hours after delivery to report that the item doesn't match its description, and states it will cancel the order and refund the buyer if the seller does not dispute the report within that window. Items bought from a Professional Seller can be returned within 14 days.

products.name: Plato's Closet
products.description: A chain of secondhand clothing stores aimed at teens and young adults. Bring items in and staff buy what they want on the spot, in cash, no shipping, listing or waiting involved. Individual stores set their own buy prices, which are not published, so no fee or payout score is given here.

accessibility.note: Plato's Closet's own site states it buys gently used teen and young adult clothes, shoes and accessories every day, no appointment necessary, and pays cash on the spot if the seller accepts the store's offer.

products.name: Goodwill
products.description: A network of independent local nonprofits that sell donated clothing in thrift stores to fund their own job training and employment programs. Donors give the clothes away and receive no cash payout, only a possible tax deduction if they itemize. Return policy varies by the roughly 150 independently run local Goodwill organizations, so no single buyer protection score is given here.

fees.note: Goodwill's own shopper page describes Goodwill as a global network of independent nonprofits that generate revenue from donated and resold goods to fund their own community job-training and employment programs, not to pay the person who donated the item.

accessibility.note: Goodwill's own site directs donors to a locator of Donation Center and Thrift Store locations across its network, where items can simply be dropped off.

products.name: Buy Nothing Project
products.description: A network of hyperlocal groups where neighbors give away clothes and other goods for free. Trading, bartering, buying or selling is against the project's own rules, so no marketplace-style buyer protection applies.

fees.note: The Buy Nothing Project's own about page states it connects neighbors 'to gift each other goods and services freely,' with no cash changing hands, and counts more than 14 million members across more than 50 countries.

accessibility.note: The Buy Nothing Project's own about page describes a network of hyperlocal groups where members give and receive through local Facebook groups or an app; joining a local group is required before posting.

products.name: The Freecycle Network
products.description: A nonprofit network of local Town groups for giving away and getting unwanted items, including clothing, with no money changing hands.

fees.note: Freecycle's own about page states membership is free and 'everything posted must be free, legal and appropriate for all ages,' so no cash payout is ever made to the person giving an item away.

accessibility.note: Freecycle's own about page states a member joins one or more local Town groups, posts what they want to gift or receive, and arranges a pickup time and location directly with the other member. It describes more than 5,000 local Town groups with over 11 million members.

products.name: Craigslist
products.description: A local classifieds site where a seller writes their own listing and arranges payment and pickup directly with a buyer. Craigslist never touches the money and takes no share of the sale price.

fees.note: Craigslist's own posting fees page lists 'All craigslist postings are free, except for' a named set of paid categories, such as job postings, some apartment rentals, commercial real estate, and for-sale-by-dealer and vehicle listings. General for-sale items posted by an individual owner are not on that paid list.

buyer_protection.note: Craigslist's own terms of use state the service is provided on an 'AS IS' and 'AS AVAILABLE' basis, that Craigslist makes no promises, warranties or representations about it, and that its own liability is capped at $100 or the amount a user paid Craigslist in the prior 12 months. There is no buyer or seller guarantee.

products.name: Fashionphile
products.description: US luxury resale company for designer handbags, accessories, jewelry and watches that buys items outright or sells them on consignment, authenticating every piece in-house before it is listed.

fees.note: Fashionphile's own consignment page says 'Our base fee is only 30% of the selling price (you keep 70%)', falling to 15% on the portion of a bag's price above $3,000, so a consignor keeps 70% on most items and more on very expensive ones. Its sell page also offers upfront buyout offers, with a 10% bonus for taking store credit instead of cash.

buyer_protection.note: Fashionphile's own authenticity page says every item is checked by a brand-specific authenticator and carries a digital certificate, and states 'We guarantee the authenticity of every ultra-luxury item we sell or 100% of your money back', calling it a lifetime guarantee. Its returns page accepts eligible returns within 15 days of delivery if the authenticity tag is still attached, with a $14.99 fee for its prepaid return label.

accessibility.note: Fashionphile's own sell page says a seller can fill in an online form and get an offer by email within 7 to 10 business days, then ship with a free label or free UPS pickup, or book an appointment at a Fashionphile location to get offers on the spot, with payment once the item is authenticated. The seller does not photograph, price or list anything.

products.name: Rebag
products.description: US luxury resale company for designer bags, watches and jewelry that gives sellers an instant price quote for most styles, and has recently added consignment, authenticating every item before it is listed.

fees.note: Rebag's own consignment page lists Rebag consignment commission rates of 8 to 35%, compared with 15 to 50% at other consignment platforms and 35 to 45% at auction houses, and says payout comes within 15 business days of the sale. A consignor therefore keeps between 65% and 92% depending on the item. Rebag's sell page separately offers an instant buyout quote for most styles.

buyer_protection.note: Rebag's own help article on authenticity says every item goes through an in-house, multilayered authentication before it is listed, and that if an item is proven inauthentic by a verified authenticator Rebag will give a full refund on return of the bag. Its return policy article allows US returns within 7 days of delivery, with a return fee of $25 to $100 per item depending on price unless the buyer is a Rebag+ member; final sale items cannot be returned. Both help pages refuse automated requests and were read in a browser and through the help center's public feed.

products.name: Hardly Ever Worn It (HEWI)
products.description: London-based peer-to-peer marketplace for pre-owned designer clothing, bags and accessories, where independent sellers list their own items after a pre-screen and a managed VIP service handles everything for larger wardrobes.

buyer_protection.note: HEWI's own help center says all listings are pre-screened for authenticity, that VIP items are physically checked in-house, and that it investigates any authenticity concern, which may include inspecting the item. On returns it says professional sellers and VIP items must accept returns within 14 days, but 'Private sellers can choose whether to accept returns', and are only obliged to when the item is not as described; seller payment is held until the buyer confirms receipt and the return period passes. No seller-fee score is given: HEWI publishes VIP commission rates (the seller keeps 60% to 90% depending on price) but none of the pages read states the commission for independent sellers.

products.name: Patagonia Worn Wear
products.description: Patagonia's own used-clothing program, which buys back its gear for store credit by mail or in its stores, then cleans, repairs and resells it online with the same guarantee as new Patagonia products.

fees.note: Patagonia's own trade-in page says 'We estimate most items’ trade-in value to be around 20% of the MSRP', with jackets worth $10 to $200, paid as credit in the form of a gift card rather than cash, and that mailing items in uses a $7 shipping label. The seller does not set a price or get a share of the eventual resale price, which puts it close to ThredUp's payout.

buyer_protection.note: Patagonia's own Worn Wear page says 'Worn Wear products are backed by the same Ironclad Guarantee as our new stuff', and that all items are inspected, authenticated, graded for condition, professionally laundered and repaired when needed before resale.

accessibility.note: Patagonia's own trade-in page offers two routes: take a quiz online, print the label and mail items in, or bring them to a Patagonia store. Items Patagonia does not accept can be sent back or recycled. There is no listing or photographing, but credit only arrives after the items are received and processed.

products.name: lululemon Like New
products.description: lululemon's own resale site for used lululemon clothing, combining items lululemon takes in by trade-in with listings from individual sellers who set their own price.

fees.note: lululemon Like New's own sell options page says an individual who lists online picks the listing price and can 'Choose 90% of sell price in credit or 70% in cash'. Its trade-in routes pay much less: 15% of the original retail price in credit, minus a $7.50 shipping fee, for mail-in, or $5 or $10 credit per item in a participating store.

buyer_protection.note: lululemon Like New's own help center says most items it sells directly can be returned online within 14 days of delivery, with $7.50 return shipping deducted from the refund, but items bought from individual sellers are final sale: the buyer can only report a misrepresented item within 3 days of delivery and ask for a refund. A separate help article says Like New items do not qualify for lululemon's Quality Promise or warranty. The help pages refuse automated requests and were read through the help center's public feed.

accessibility.note: lululemon Like New's own sell options page says items brought to a participating store are processed on the spot for instant credit, while the mail-in route takes about three weeks and online listings typically sell in two to three weeks.

products.name: Sellpy
products.description: European mail-in consignment service: the seller fills a Sellpy bag with clothes, Sellpy photographs, prices and sells each item online and pays the seller a share.

fees.note: Sellpy's own German pricing page says the seller receives 40% of the part of the sale price under 50 euros and 70% of the part above it, minus a listing fee of 1.30 euros per item, that a Sellpy bag costs 3.50 euros and that returning rejected items costs 4.99 euros. On a 10-euro item the seller keeps about 4 euros before the listing fee, close to ThredUp's payout on low-priced items. The page also carries a notice of new prices from 2 November without saying which year; the figures here are those it showed in October 2026.

buyer_protection.note: Sellpy's own EU terms of purchase add 16 days to the 14-day withdrawal right in EU law so that 'you have a total of 30 days to make a return for any reason at all', with a return shipping charge deducted from the refund unless stated otherwise. Because Sellpy itself is the seller to the buyer, the buyer is not dealing with a private individual.

accessibility.note: Sellpy's own German selling pages describe ordering a Sellpy bag, filling it and sending it with a free shipping label, after which Sellpy handles listing, pricing and sale; the seller does not photograph or list each item.

products.name: Oxfam shops and Online Shop
products.description: UK charity's network of high street secondhand shops and its Online Shop, which resell donated clothing, books and household goods to raise money for Oxfam's work against poverty. Donors receive no payment.

fees.note: Oxfam's own page on donating to its charity shops asks for unwanted items that it can 'turn into life-changing cash' for its work against poverty; the person donating receives no payment, scored here the same way as Goodwill.

buyer_protection.note: The Oxfam Online Shop's own FAQ says it offers a 28-day returns policy on all products except Unwrapped gift cards, and that from 3 February 2026 a £2.95 fee per returned parcel is deducted from the refund. Because Oxfam is the seller, the buyer is dealing with a trader rather than a private individual.

accessibility.note: Oxfam's own donation page says donations are welcome at its charity shops in England, Wales and Scotland and can also be sent by post, and lists the clothing, shoes, accessories and household goods its shops can sell. Dropping items at a shop involves no listing or shipping.
